description: The `config` object of an enabled `api_chargeback` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component ApiChargebackConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

ApiChargebackConfig.description:
Plugin: api_chargeback — Per-consumer API usage charge tracking across
three independent pricing dimensions: per-call pricing by billable
status code, per-byte bandwidth pricing (both client->backend and
backend->client, applied to HTTP-family AND stream proxies), and
per-connection pricing for stream proxies (TCP/TCP+TLS/UDP/DTLS).
Ordinary HTTP uses the wire status. Native gRPC and translated
gRPC-Web use the final client-visible grpc-status mapped to the
canonical effective HTTP status; missing/malformed/unknown terminal
status, and a terminal status present on the wire but unreadable by the
gateway, fail closed to 500. Explicitly zero-priced tiers still meter calls.
Bandwidth pricing bills WebSocket sessions from the parsed relay's
payload byte counters, so a bandwidth-priced instance keeps its proxy's
WebSocket sessions off the raw tunnel relay and is refused on a
`websocket_permessage_deflate: passthrough` proxy.
Successful H1/H2/H3 WebSocket handshakes share the 101 pricing tier;
rejected handshakes retain their error status.
At least one of `pricing_tiers`, `bandwidth_pricing`, or
`stream_connection_pricing` must be configured.
Unknown top-level keys and unknown `pricing_tiers[]` keys are
rejected so a misspelled pricing dimension cannot silently bill
at zero.
Exactly-once accounting: after scope merging, each proxy may retain
at most one effective `api_chargeback` instance. Multiple proxy-scoped,
proxy-group-scoped, or mixed attachments on one proxy are rejected
because the process-global `/charges` registry has no ledger/instance
dimension. Distinct proxies may each attach one instance (including
different currencies/pricing). Shared render/cleanup/budget tunables
(`render_cache_ttl_seconds`, `stale_entry_ttl_seconds`,
`cache_invalidation_min_age_ms`, `cleanup_interval_seconds`,
`max_entries`, `max_retained_bytes`) must
agree across every enabled instance in the process.
Cardinality budget: the shared registry retains at most `max_entries`
billing rows (complete registry entry keys) and at most
`max_retained_bytes` of state. Keys include consumer, proxy, status,
protocol family, currency, namespace, and prices, so one principal can
occupy many slots. A new ordinary row beyond either ceiling uses its
prepared aggregate fallback, preserving totals while losing per-identity
attribution. Outside a prepared matrix, an aggregate that cannot reserve
bytes drops the charge and increments `dropped_charges_total`. The
aggregate `consumer` label is the internal sentinel
`__cardinality_overflow__~sha256:ferrum-edge/api-chargeback/overflow/v1`,
preserving billable totals while losing only per-identity attribution.
The aggregate overflow rows are created and their missing bytes reserved
atomically while staging, before the cache generation can serve. There
is one row per priced status, one shared status-0 bandwidth row when
bandwidth is priced, or one row per stream proxy. Global instances also
reserve unknown-proxy fallback rows in their own and all known namespaces.
Rows stay pinned while a cache generation owns them; unused preallocations
consume estimated bytes but do not appear as billing series. Ordinary
admission leaves an additional matrix of reload headroom. This cannot
guarantee that a larger matrix or repeated repricing fits beside history.
That sentinel lives in the digest-form billing-identity class, so a real
authenticated or configured identity can never share its registry key.
Billing identities are never prefix-truncated: an external identity
claim above 512 bytes is rejected at authentication, and any remaining
oversized value is represented as a prefix plus a domain-separated
SHA-256 digest of the complete value.
Runtime-only admission (not expressible here): every enabled instance
must resolve to the same shared tunables and the same projection; a
`schema_ref` must name a definition a `transaction_log_schema` plugin
registered; a status code must not appear in more than one tier across
the whole `pricing_tiers` array; `max_retained_bytes` must hold twice
the configured overflow-row matrix, and a reload whose not-yet-created
overflow rows do not fit beside the billing state the live registry
retains is refused wholesale when a node builds that generation (not by
offline validation). This includes a budget-lowering reload needing new
fallback rows; if every fallback row already exists, a lower budget is
accepted and existing state drains through eviction. Current aggregate
rows and their cumulative exported series remain retained while pinned.
`stale_entry_ttl_seconds` /
`cleanup_interval_seconds` interact with the collection contract
described in docs/plugins.md.

currency.description:
Currency label included in Prometheus metrics and JSON output.
Informational only — the plugin does not perform currency
conversion. Trimmed at admission and rejected when the trimmed
value is empty, so a whitespace-only label cannot become a currency.

status_codes.description: Billable status codes that trigger this tier's charge. Must be real HTTP status codes in 100–599 and distinct within the tier. Ordinary HTTP uses the wire status. Native gRPC and translated gRPC-Web map final terminal codes as 0→200, 1→499, 2→500, 3→400, 4→504, 5→404, 6→409, 7→403, 8→429, 9→400, 10→409, 11→400, 12→501, 13→500, 14→503, 15→500, and 16→401; missing, malformed, unknown, or present-but-unreadable terminal codes map to 500. A status code must appear in exactly one tier; cross-tier duplication is rejected at construction.

price_per_call.description:
Charge per HTTP API call (e.g. 0.00001). Must be finite,
non-negative, and at most 1e288 so `u64` counter × price stays
finite in IEEE-754 binary64. Stored counters are converted to
binary64 before multiplication, so values above 2^53 follow
normal binary64 rounding; Ferrum applies no additional decimal
rounding. Prometheus formats 10 fractional digits.

pricing_tiers.description:
HTTP-family per-call pricing. Each tier maps a set of billable
status codes to a per-call price. Ordinary HTTP uses its wire
status; native gRPC and translated gRPC-Web use the canonical
effective-HTTP mapping of the finalized terminal grpc-status.
Stream proxies (TCP/UDP/DTLS) have no HTTP status code and use
`stream_connection_pricing` instead.

bandwidth_pricing.description:
Optional bandwidth pricing applied to both HTTP-family and stream
transactions, using the gateway-perspective `bytes_sent` /
`bytes_received` counters from the transaction-summary schema.
WebSocket sessions are billed from the parsed relay's payload byte
counters; any nonzero price keeps the proxy's WebSocket sessions on
the parsed relay (no raw tunnel copy) and is refused on a
`websocket_permessage_deflate: passthrough` proxy.

price_per_byte_sent.description:
Per-byte charge for bytes flowed client->backend. Finite,
non-negative, at most 1e288 (same binary64 counter×price bound
as `price_per_call`).

price_per_byte_received.description:
Per-byte charge for bytes flowed backend->client. Finite,
non-negative, at most 1e288 (same binary64 counter×price bound
as `price_per_call`).

stream_connection_pricing.description:
Optional per-connection pricing for stream proxies (TCP, TCP+TLS,
UDP, DTLS). Charges the configured flat fee once per session at
disconnect time. Streams have no HTTP status code so they cannot
use `pricing_tiers`.

price_per_connection.description:
Per-session charge applied at stream disconnect. Finite,
non-negative, at most 1e288 (same binary64 counter×price bound
as `price_per_call`).

render_cache_ttl_seconds.description:
How long the cached /charges response is served before rebuilding.
Unsigned 64-bit; a negative or fractional value is rejected at
construction. Process-global: every enabled api_chargeback instance
must use the same value.

stale_entry_ttl_seconds.description:
How long an idle chargeback entry may live before it becomes
eligible for eviction. Eligibility is not deletion: an idle entry is
removed only once two delivered GET /charges exports (the admin
connection took the complete document) have collected its current
counters, and only together with every row sharing its consumer,
proxy, and currency, so uncollected billing state is never discarded
on age alone and a live cumulative series never shrinks. Unsigned
64-bit. Process-global: every enabled
api_chargeback instance must use the same value.

cache_invalidation_min_age_ms.description:
Minimum age (ms) of a render cache before record() will invalidate
it. Evaluated per format against that document's own timestamp, so
a JSON-only collector gets the same protection as a Prometheus one.
Unsigned 64-bit. Process-global: every enabled api_chargeback
instance must use the same value.

cleanup_interval_seconds.description:
How often (seconds) the background task evicts entries that have
been idle longer than stale_entry_ttl_seconds AND have already been
confirmed collected by two delivered exports. Set to 0 to disable. At most
31536000 (one year); larger values are rejected because the task's
sleep deadline would overflow. Process-global: every enabled
api_chargeback instance must use the same value.

max_entries.description:
Hard ceiling on retained billing rows (complete registry entry keys)
in the shared /charges registry. One principal can occupy many slots
because keys also include proxy, status, protocol family, currency,
namespace, and prices. Charges for a new row beyond this ceiling are
folded into the fixed-cardinality internal overflow aggregate row
(`__cardinality_overflow__~sha256:ferrum-edge/api-chargeback/overflow/v1`)
when its prepared fallback exists — per-identity attribution is lost
while recorded totals are preserved. A charge outside a prepared
matrix may be dropped if no aggregate can reserve bytes; inspect
dropped_charges_total. 0 is rejected — there is no unlimited mode.
Process-global: every enabled api_chargeback instance must use the
same value.

max_retained_bytes.description:
Hard ceiling on estimated retained registry bytes, covering ordinary
billing rows and aggregate overflow rows together. The overflow rows
the configured proxies and pricing tiers can create are reserved
and created during cache staging, plus equal headroom for a pricing
reload. Admission refuses a budget that cannot hold twice that matrix.
A node also refuses the whole reload if missing fallback rows cannot
fit beside retained state under the candidate budget, including a
budget decrease needing new rows. A decrease with all rows already
present is allowed and drains existing state through eviction. Charges
outside a prepared matrix can still be dropped when a new aggregate
cannot reserve bytes; inspect dropped_charges_total. 0 is rejected.
Process-global: every enabled api_chargeback instance must use the
same value.

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. Projects the per-proxy billing row inside the `GET /charges` document (`proxy_id`, `namespace`, `proxy_name`, `currency`, `protocol_family`, `total_calls`, `total_charges`, `by_status`, `bandwidth`, `stream`). Billing identity, charge accounting, registry keys, and the Prometheus exposition are unaffected. `summary_type`, `timestamp_format`, `metadata`, `order`, `transforms`, and every derived kind except `summary_kind` are rejected for this surface. Process-global: every enabled api_chargeback instance must resolve to the same projection because one render cache serves them all. See docs/log_schema.md.

ApiChargebackRenderSchema.description: `SummaryLogSchema` narrowed to what an `api_chargeback` billing row can actually express. The `/charges` row is an aggregate assembled into a `serde_json::Map`-backed document, so it has no HTTP/stream summary type, no RFC3339 timestamp field, no metadata map, and no member order under the projection's control: `summary_type`, `timestamp_format`, `metadata`, `order`, and `transforms` are rejected at construction rather than silently ignored. `omit` names and `rename` sources must be native billing-row fields, and `summary_kind` is the only derived kind representable from a row that spans many transactions (it has no single status, backend, or outcome). See docs/log_schema.md.

SummaryLogSchema.description: Customizable output schema for transaction-log JSON / line protocol. Rename keys, drop fields, reorder, inject static stamping, emit derived fields, flatten metadata. Metadata redaction always applies on every code path — sensitive substrings (`authorization`, `cookie`, `password`, `token`, …) cannot be introduced via `static_fields` or `derived_fields` (rejected at construction). This object, each `derived_fields` entry, and `metadata` are strict fixed shapes: unknown keys are rejected with a nested path. HTTP summaries include the normalized terminal `grpc_status` field (separate from `response_status_code`) when the request is gRPC. It can be renamed, omitted, or ordered like every other native field. `api_chargeback`, `api_chargeback_sink`, and `transaction_debugger` reuse this same shape against their own record families; whatever a family cannot express (`summary_type`, `timestamp_format`, `metadata`, `order`, or a derived kind with no source field) is rejected at construction with a plugin- and field-specific diagnostic. Constraints this document cannot express are still enforced at construction and are NOT relaxations of the runtime contract: `omit` / `rename` / `order` names must resolve against the record family's field inventory for the selected `summary_type`; a field may not be both omitted and renamed; the combined native, static, and derived output keys must be unique; `order` must list every non-extension output key unless it contains `"*"`; and `rename` targets, `static_fields` keys (including nested keys) and `derived_fields` names may not match a sensitive-data substring or a credential-class name (for example `session_id`, `client_assertion`, `gpg_passphrase`, `private_rsa_key`; see docs/log_schema.md), while a `static_fields` string value that looks like a literal HTTP auth credential is refused. Under `metadata.mode: flatten`, `omit` may not list `metadata` and `rename` may not rename it; under `metadata.mode: omit`, `rename` may not rename it (those directives would otherwise be silently ignored). The whole `static_fields` object serialized as JSON (escaped keys and values, quotes, separators, braces) must be at most 16384 bytes and a static value may nest at most 8 objects/arrays deep. `transforms` keys must be fields of the selected `summary_type`, may not also be omitted, `ip_prefix` applies only to `client_ip` / `backend_resolved_ip`, and a `hash` `secret_ref` must resolve to a set `FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>` value of at least 32 bytes. See docs/log_schema.md.

summary_type.description: Which summary type(s) this schema applies to. Summaries of the other type fall back to native serialization (the schema only customizes types it claims to handle).

omit.description: Native field names to drop from output.

rename.description: Map of native field name -> output key (at most 128 bytes).

order.description: Explicit output order, by output key. May contain `"*"` once as a wildcard for "every unlisted entry in natural order." Without `"*"`, every field must be listed. Entries are unique — a repeated output key (or a second `"*"`) is rejected.

static_fields.description: Literal JSON values injected at top level. Keys / nested keys matching sensitive substrings or credential-class names (for example `session_id`) are rejected at compile time. A `null` value is rejected — use `omit` to drop a field. At most 64 entries; keys are at most 128 bytes; the whole object serialized as JSON (escaped keys and values included) is at most 16384 bytes; a value nests at most 8 objects/arrays deep. Static fields are stamped into every record, so these bounds are a per-record cost cap.

derived_fields.description: Computed values; emitted alongside native fields.

name.description: Output key for the derived value.

kind.description: `status_class`: `"1xx"`–`"5xx"` from `response_status_code` (stream: `"none"`). `backend_host`: hostname from `backend_target` (port stripped, IPv6 brackets honored). `summary_kind`: `"http"`, `"stream"`, or `"websocket_disconnect"` (the last only for `ws_logging` WebSocket disconnect entries). `outcome`: `"ok"` / `"error"`.

prefix.description: Prepended to each metadata key when promoted to top-level (e.g. `"meta_"`); only `flatten` reads it. Control characters are rejected. The type and the control-character restriction are validated in every mode, so a `nested` or `omit` schema cannot carry a value that would only start failing once the mode is switched to `flatten`.

on_collision.description: Behavior when a metadata key collides with an already-emitted field; only `flatten` reads it. `skip` keeps the existing value; `overwrite` replaces the colliding field's value in place with the (redacted) metadata value, so every key appears exactly once in the record. Validated in every mode, like `prefix`.

timestamp_format.description: Conversion applied to timestamp string fields (`timestamp_received`, `timestamp_connected`, `timestamp_disconnected`). Parse failures fall back to the raw RFC3339 string.

transforms.description: Per-field value transforms, keyed by native source field name (before `rename`), applied when the field is emitted: `truncate` keeps at most `max_bytes` bytes (cut on a UTF-8 boundary); `ip_prefix` keeps the network prefix of an IP address (`ipv4_bits` default 24, `ipv6_bits` default 48; IPv4-mapped IPv6 is masked as IPv4; a value that is not an address is emitted as `null`); `hash` replaces the value with the lowercase-hex keyed HMAC-SHA-256 under the secret named by `secret_ref`, which must be a `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` reference resolved at construction (literal secrets are refused; the value must be at least 32 bytes). Only the transaction-summary loggers support `transforms`; `api_chargeback`, `api_chargeback_sink`, and `transaction_debugger` reject the key, and statsd ignores it. Kafka partition keys and Loki labels read typed fields and are not transformed.
